Getting a Shot When Needles Scare You

Open this before a vaccination, a blood draw or any appointment with a needle in it, when the dread has been building for days. It lists the things you can ask for and do that make the minute itself much easier.

Needles · Anxiety · Body · Grounding · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Say at the desk that needles are hard for you — Staff do this all day and will slow down if they know.
  • Ask to lie down rather than sit — Lying flat makes feeling faint far less likely.
  • Eat and drink something beforehand — Going in hungry or dry makes everything feel worse.
  • Look away and pick something to study — Watching the needle gives your body more to react to.
  • Breathe out slowly as it goes in — A long out-breath settles the whole system for a few seconds.
  • Tense and release your legs a few times — Squeezing and releasing your muscles helps you stay steady.
  • Ask for a few minutes before standing — Getting up straight away is where people come unstuck.
  • Plan one small good thing for after — Something to walk toward changes what you are focused on.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
